FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Buider’s 
Hardware Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 


Door stoppers with durable rubber ends come in various designs or shapes and are used to help keep the doors 
open as needed as well as to avoid damages on account of unwanted slamming of door. This standard has been 
formulated to provide guidance to the manufacturers and users of stainless steel door stoppers which are viable 
even in coastal areas and/or in humid weather. This standard covers classification, and requirements relating 
to materials, sizes, manufacture, finish, sampling and criteria for conformity, packing and marking of the door 
stoppers. 

The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex B. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17296 : 2020 


Indian Standard 


STAINLESS STEEL DOOR STOPPERS — 
SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard covers requirements for materials, 
dimensions, manufacture and finish of stainless steel 
door stoppers. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which 
through reference in the text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and the parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below: 


IS No. Title 
6527: 1995 Stainless steel wire rod — 
Specification 
6760: 1972 Specification for slotted countersunk 
head wood screws 
6911:2017 Stainless steel plate, sheet and 


strip — Specification 


3 CLASSIFICATION 


Stainless steel door stoppers shall be of the following 
types: 

a) Single rod door stoppers; 

b) Double rod door stoppers; and 

c) Long square rod door stoppers. 


4 MATERIAL 


4.1 The material for manufacture of door stoppers shall 
be as given in 4.1.1 to 4.1.3. However, any advanced 
material (stainless steel or rubber) material may also be 
used as per the agreement between manufacturer and 
the purchaser as per the relevant Indian Standards, in 
which case the material along with its correspondence 
to the concerned Indian Standard shall be marked on 
the packing. 


4.1.1 Base Plate 


The stainless steel for base plate shall conform to any 
suitable grade of IS 6911. 


4.1.2 Rod 


The stainless steel for rod shall conform to any suitable 
grade of IS 6527. 


4.1.3 Rubber 


The rubber piece attached on the extreme end shall 
comply with the shore hardness 60 + 5A. 


5 SIZES 


5.1 The sizes of door stoppers shall be denoted by 
overall height, Z as shown in Fig. 1, Fig. 2 and Fig. 3. 


5.2 The dimensions and tolerances of various types of 
stainless steel door stoppers shall be as given in Fig. 
1, Fig. 2 and Fig. 3. However, the shapes shown are 
typical in nature. 


6 MANUFACTURE 


6.1 General 


Door stoppers shall be well made and free from flaws 
and defects of any kind. All the stoppers shall be cut 
and finished clean and shall be provided with stainless 
steel rod pressed and riveted strongly to provide proper 
fitment without any looseness. 


The rubber part shall be screwed in or suitably fixed 
with good quality adhesive into the rod to give strong 
fitment. The rod in the barrel may have a provision of 
tiny steel ball for the effective movement to avoid free 
drop of the stopper. 


6.2 Screw Holes 


All the screw holes shall be clean and suitable for 
countersunk head of wood screws as given in Fig. 1, 
Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 (see IS 6760 for screw size). Steel 
screws may be used for use with steel doors as per the 
relevant Indian Standards. 


6.2.1 Number of Screw Holes 
The door stopper shall have minimum of 4 screw holes 
in the base plate to have better fitment. 


7 FINISH 


The door stoppers shall be finished satin or bright with 
smooth surface. Other finish as agreed to between the 
manufacturer and the purchaser may also be provided. 


S SAMPLING AND 
CONFORMITY 


CRITERIA FOR 


The method of sampling door stoppers and the criteria 
for conformity shall be as given in Annex A.

9 MARKING 


9.1 Each door stopper shall be legibly and indelibly 
marked with the following: 


a) Manufacturer name or trade-mark; and 
b) Size of the door stopper. 


9.2 Similar information shall be provided in the 
delivery advices accompanying the shipment of packed 
cardboard boxes as well (see 10.1). 


9.3 BIS Certification Marking 


The products(s) conforming to the requirement of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the products(s) 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


10 PACKING 


10.1 Each door stopper duly wrapped in polyethylene 
or other suitable bag shall be suitably packed in a 
cardboard box in multiples of 5. 


10.2 Each cardboard box shall be marked with the 
following information: 


a) Manufacturer’s name and trade-mark, if any; 
b) Address of the manufacturer; 
c) Type and finish of door stopper; 


d) Details of materials used including their grade/ 
type, etc and relevant Indian Standards; 


e) Size of door stopper; 
f) Quantity; 

g) Date of manufacture; 
h) Country of origin; and 
3) Batch/lot number. 


IS 17296 : 2020

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: CED 15 (13629).
